maria (ML): Quick share — ran a focused weight-only INT8 run using bitsandbytes/load_in_8bit on rwlm-13b-v1. Wanted to capture perf vs quality tradeoffs and ask for ideas.

akash (infra): Nice. TL;DR numbers up front? and what bitsandbytes version / load flags did you use? :eyes:

maria (ML): TL;DR: peak GPU mem from ~23.6GB -> 7.8GB (≈3x reduction), token throughput +15% (12.3k -> 14.1k toks/s), MMLU 73.1 -> 71.5 (−1.6 pts). Wikitext ppl +0.9. Some systematic failure modes on multi-step math and a few factuals. bitsandbytes 0.39, load_in_8bit=True, device_map='auto'. Command I ran:

```bash
python eval_runner.py \
  --model redwood/rwlm-13b-v1 \
  --load_in_8bit True \
  --bnb-version 0.39 \
  --batch 4 \
  --prompt-set mmlu,wikitext,our_regression_suite
```

ben (runtime): Interesting. p95 latency numbers? and are those throughput numbers single-GPU? Also did you use KV cache offload or anything special?

maria (ML): Single A100-40G. p50 ~62ms/token fp16 -> ~58ms/token int8; p95 ~120ms -> ~118ms (no major latency regressions). KV cache kept on GPU; no CPU-offload. All numbers are evac eval scripts (single stream micro-batching for throughput).

akash (infra): The mem drop is great. Any issues with stability/crashes or instabilities during long streams? :thinking_face:

maria (ML): Ran 24h soak with mixed traffic pattern, no OOMs. A few cases of output stuttering (repeats) on long generation; might be quantization noise accumulating.

sophia (evals): Can you paste 1-2 examples of the failure modes? we should add targeted test prompts.

maria (ML): Example (shortened):
"Q: Explain step-by-step how to compute 37*24."
FP16: correct multi-step reasoning.
INT8: produces an incorrect intermediate, then repeats last two steps and ends with wrong answer.

akash (infra): Did you try layerwise fallback to FP16 for outlier layers? there's been wins on other models.

ben (runtime): We can detect outlier layers by measuring per-linear activation ranges and fallback to FP16 for layers with high outlier ratios. I prototyped a quick toggle:

```py
# pseudo
outlier_layers = detect_outliers(model, thresh=3.5)
for l in outlier_layers:
    quantize_layer(l, keep_fp16=True)
```

ben (runtime): That tends to keep most of the mem gains but recovers some accuracy for math-like reasoning.

maria (ML): Good idea. I tried forcing last 6 transformer layers to FP16 and MMLU improved to 72.6 (got ~1.1 pts back) while peak mem stayed ~9.5GB. So tradeoff seems promising.

sophia (evals): How does this compare to other weight-only schemes (GPTQ/AWQ) you tried? We should pick baseline set to compare.

maria (ML): Ran quick GPTQ/GGUF and AWQ runs as well: GPTQ (8-bit group-wise) gave MMLU 72.8, but quantize+deploy pipeline is slower (takes ~6h vs bitsandbytes instant load). AWQ matched GPTQ quality-ish but needs custom kernels; throughput was slightly worse than bnb-int8. So bitsandbytes load_in_8bit wins for deploy simplicity + throughput, GPTQ/AWQ slightly better on quality but heavier infra/serving work.

akash (infra): Notes for infra — GPTQ artifacts need custom op support and larger cold-start memory for the converter step. Bitsandbytes path is easier for self-serve Dedicated/Hosted.

ben (runtime): We should also test with llm.int8() style fused ops (if available) + group size tweaks. Group size (g=128 vs 64) changes error profile a lot.

maria (ML): Yep, tried group size 64 -> slightly better quality (MMLU 71.9) but a bit more mem. I also toggled per-channel scales and symmetric vs asymmetric quant; per-channel wins.

sophia (evals): Can you add the regression prompts and diff outputs to the eval repo? I'll run fine-grained metrics (math/commonsense/fact recall) and produce a report.

maria (ML): Will upload diffs to the evals bucket + add a small reproduction script. For next runs I'll try: (1) auto-detect outlier layers + FP16 fallback, (2) bnb group-size sweep, (3) gated GPTQ on top-k layers.

deploy-bot: @channel smoke test request: schedule a small smoke on dedicated-small (8g) next Tue 10:00 PT. Tagging infra.

akash (infra): noted — I'll reserve the node and add a perf job that runs fp16/int8/partial-fp16 for side-by-side logs. :thumbsup:

maria (ML): Thanks all — will post the artifact + numbers once uploads finish. If anyone wants to hack the outlier detection script ping me and I'll share the notebook. :partyparrot:
